official.deadline_note: Two cycles a year. First cycle opens 1 November and closes 1 February of the following year (next close 1 February 2027); second cycle opens 1 June and closes 10 August. A*GA may consider off-cycle applications on a case-by-case basis. Note that the A*STAR scholarships directory page states the AGS 'Application Deadline: 15 February and 10 August', so the February close date is published differently on two official A*STAR pages.

official.status_note: As at 10 October 2026 the second 2026 cycle (1 June to 10 August 2026) has closed, with outcomes notified from mid-November; the next cycle opens on 1 November. A*GA may still consider off-cycle applications case-by-case.

official.application_route: Create an account on the A*STAR scholarship applicant portal after securing an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty co-supervisor plus the A*STAR supervisor's endorsement, and apply for PhD admission at an autonomous university at the same time.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to applicants of all nationalities. International Students applying must have completed or be on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a Singapore Autonomous University (AU). Singaporeans and Singapore Permanent Residents have no service commitment; foreigners who are non-SPRs serve a 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies (local companies and international companies with a base in Singapore registered with ACRA), without commitment to any specific organisation.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - all nationalities may apply, but international students must have completed or be on track to obtain a Bachelor's or Master's degree from a Singapore Autonomous University, and non-SPR international awardees serve a 3-year service commitment in a Singapore-based company, with work preferably in Biomedical Sciences, Physical Sciences, Engineering or Computing and Information Sciences.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Four tracks: STEM (biomedical sciences, chemistry, physics, engineering and related fields), Semiconductor (chip design, materials science, semiconductor technologies), Quantum (quantum computing, communications, sensing) and Computing (AI, cybersecurity, software engineering, data science). Published research areas include antimicrobial resistance, bioinformatics, food science, infectious diseases, MedTech, metabolic and brain health, precision and preventive health, synthetic biology, therapeutics, data/AI and compute, quantum, semiconductors, smart and sustainable advanced manufacturing, sustainable energy and chemicals, automated hub operations and real-time resilient and optimised supply chain. The list is not exhaustive.
official.research_requirement: Yes - applicants must develop a research proposal in consultation with both supervisors that aligns with their research interests and contributes to Singapore's RIE ecosystem, and obtain A*STAR supervisor endorsement confirming the PhD research will be conducted in whole or in part at the relevant A*STAR Research Institute.
official.description: A*STAR frames AGS as offering full funding, access to world-class research labs and the chance to take on a 12-month overseas attachment during the PhD, funding up to four years of PhD or EngD study at an autonomous university in Singapore with joint supervision by an A*STAR researcher and a university faculty member. Scholars begin their research journey at an A*STAR Research Institute and, after completing their PhD or EngD, may apply for the A*STAR International Fellowship for post-doctoral training at top overseas universities.
official.program_type: Government scholarship - A*STAR Graduate Academy graduate scholarship

applicant_utility.summary: AGS is the strongest route into an A*STAR Research Institute for a Singapore-based PhD, paying full tuition plus a monthly sustenance allowance of SGD 3,600 to SGD 6,200 depending on track and residency, but the award is conditional on already having two named supervisors who have signed on. International applicants are the narrowest group: you must already hold, or be about to complete, a degree from a Singapore autonomous university, and if you are not a Singapore Permanent Resident you take on a three-year service commitment in an ACRA-registered Singapore-based company afterwards. Because the process runs roughly five months from a complete application to an outcome, the practical deadline is several weeks before the published closing date, not the date itself.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-semester undergraduates or Master's students at a Singapore autonomous university with a Second Upper who have already identified an A*STAR PI willing to co-supervise, plus mid-PhD students at a Singapore AU looking to switch onto funded A*STAR supervision.
application_readiness_checklist: Approach an A*STAR Principal Investigator or Principal Scientist and a university faculty member months in advance and confirm both are willing to collaborate and co-supervise before you touch the application form
Confirm your prospective co-supervisor is already approved as an AGS supervisor, or ask them to check with their university or RI Human Resources about the approval process
Write the research proposal jointly with both supervisors so it reads as contributing to Singapore's RIE ecosystem, not as a standalone academic idea
Submit the partner-university PhD application in the same window as the scholarship application - the award lapses without confirmed placement
Line up at least two academic referees (your current university supervisor must be one of them for mid-term applicants) and warn them that reports are due within days of submission
Prepare your CV before you create the account, since the portal expects it at registration
common_rejection_risks: Applying without a confirmed, A*STAR-approved co-supervisor - supervisor approval and project endorsement are gating steps, not formalities
Leaving the university admission application late so the scholarship offer expires before placement is confirmed
Referee reports not submitted in time, which leaves the application incomplete and stops the clock on the roughly five-month process
A research proposal that does not connect to an A*STAR research area or to Singapore's RIE priorities
Missing the Second-Class (Upper) threshold with nothing else in the file - A*STAR does assess holistically, but a Second Class Lower alone is a weak position
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: A*STAR does not pay for consumables or research fees; lab fees are borne by the university. The page does not publish travel or airfare allowances for the 12-month overseas attachment, any settling-in allowance, or accommodation support, so flights to Singapore, housing, insurance and day-to-day costs above the monthly sustenance allowance sit with the scholar. Doctoral candidates must also fund anything beyond the four-year funding period, which requires A*STAR management approval for a PhD extension.
document_audit: Referee reports are not uploads - each nominated referee receives an auto-generated email with a link, so referees who miss it silently break your file

The A*STAR supervisor endorsement is a bundle of five separate written confirmations, not a single signature: project summary, willingness to co-supervise, reasons for supporting you, the rationale for the university collaboration, and confirmation the research happens at least partly at the A*STAR RI
All academic credentials must be in the file, not just the highest degree - mid-term applicants need current enrolment evidence too
Your CV must exist before you create the application account
alerts: The February closing date is published as 1 February on the AGS page but as 15 February on the A*STAR scholarships directory page - treat 1 February as your working deadline and confirm with A*GA

International students who are not Singapore Permanent Residents take a 3-year service commitment in Singapore-based companies after the PhD, with work preferably in biomedical sciences, physical sciences, engineering or computing and information sciences
Mid-term applicants receive the same terms from the point of award but with retrospective payment of tuition and compulsory fees from Year 1, so timing of the application affects back pay
All rates and allowances are explicitly subject to adjustment by A*STAR from time to time
Changing your course of study or research project mid-PhD requires A*STAR's written permission and is assessed case by case
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online account creation on the A*STAR applicant portal, complete application with documents and referee nominations, then at least two interview rounds with BMRC or SERC senior management and A*STAR Research Entity researchers, with outcome by email roughly five months after a complete application.

official.application_route: Tick the scholarship interest inside the NUS graduate admissions application in GradApp and complete the additional scholarship requirements listed there; there is no separate scholarship form.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to Singapore Citizens, Singapore Permanent Residents and All International Students. The Scholarship is tenable only at the National University of Singapore and the Scholar must reside in Singapore for the duration of the Scholarship.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - all international students are eligible for the SGD 3,000 per month PhD rate or SGD 2,900 per month Master's (Research) rate, but international scholars must fulfil the Graduate Assistantship Programme requirements (416 hours for a PhD, 156 hours for a 2-year Master's by Research, 78 hours for a 1-year Master's by Research) and must be eligible for the MOE tuition fee subsidy.
official.research_requirement: Yes - the Scholarship is awarded to outstanding graduate students for research leading to a higher degree at the University, and holders must be offered admission to a full-time graduate research programme.
official.duration: Typical award period 4 years for PhD students and 2 years for Master's (Research) students; tenable for one year in the first instance and renewable each semester, with a maximum period of two years for Master's candidates and four years for PhD candidates as determined by the relevant faculty or school.
official.description: The NUS Research Scholarship is awarded by the NUS Graduate School to outstanding graduate students for research leading to a higher degree at the University, combining a full waiver of tuition fees with a monthly stipend that varies by citizenship status and degree. PhD scholars who pass the PhD Qualifying Examination may receive an additional stipend of up to SGD 500 per month, and the award is applied for within the NUS graduate admissions application.
official.program_type: Research-based graduate scholarship - NUS Graduate School
official.english_requirement: For non-native English speakers, proficiency demonstrated through tests like TOEFL or IELTS, listed by NUSGS as an optional supporting item (items 5-7 are optional).

applicant_utility.summary: The NUS Research Scholarship is a full tuition waiver plus a monthly stipend of SGD 2,900 to SGD 3,800 depending on your degree and citizenship, and there is no separate scholarship deadline because you claim it inside the GradApp admissions application. International PhD scholars receive SGD 3,000 per month, rising by up to SGD 500 once the Qualifying Examination is passed, but must also serve 416 hours of Graduate Assistantship work during candidature. Treat the faculty application deadline, not a scholarship deadline, as your real cut-off, and check the MOE tuition-fee-subsidy requirement before you rely on this for budgeting.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Research master's and PhD applicants with at least a Second Upper degree who have a supervisor or faculty in mind at NUS and want tuition covered while they focus on research.
application_readiness_checklist: Find the application deadline on your target faculty's own website, since NUSGS deliberately does not publish one for the August or January intake
Confirm you are eligible for the MOE tuition fee subsidy before treating the tuition waiver as guaranteed - non-subsidised applicants cannot hold the scholarship
Secure admission to a full-time graduate research programme first or concurrently; the award requires an offer at the time of award
Tick the scholarship interest and 'Source of Finance' field inside GradApp rather than looking for a separate scholarship form
Submit a GRE score even though it is optional - NUSGS states quantitative, verbal and analytical evidence significantly strengthens the application
Budget the 416 hours (PhD) or 156/78 hours (research master's) of Graduate Assistantship work into your first-year schedule if you are an international scholar
common_rejection_risks: Missing the faculty application deadline while waiting for a scholarship deadline that does not exist
Not being eligible for the MOE tuition fee subsidy, which removes the tuition waiver and the scholarship itself
A statement of purpose that reads as generic rather than mapping research interests, career aspirations and motivation for the specific programme
Thin referee letters, since the compulsory file is GPA, statement of purpose, recommendation letters and CV with little else to offset weak references
Expecting the award to run the full four or two years automatically - renewal is each semester and depends on satisfactory progress and the University's discretion
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Miscellaneous Student Fees are deducted from the monthly stipend at the beginning of each semester, and the University explicitly provides no additional assistance towards travel or living costs and no travel or other allowances, so airfare to Singapore, accommodation, insurance and everyday living expenses come out of the stipend. The stipend itself is not subject to income tax, and CPF is paid on top only for Singapore Citizens.
document_audit: MOE tuition-fee-subsidy eligibility is a separate gate from admission - verify it early, it is not part of the standard admissions checklist
Referees can be academic or professional, but NUSGS assesses research skills and experience heavily, so academic referees who can speak to research output carry more weight
GRE, publication and TOEFL/IELTS evidence are formally optional, yet NUSGS says these items significantly strengthen the application - omitting all three weakens the file
The scholarship is renewable each semester rather than guaranteed for the full period, so keep a record of progress reports and supervisor sign-offs
alerts: International scholars must serve 416 hours (PhD), 156 hours (2-year Master's by Research) or 78 hours (1-year Master's by Research) under the Graduate Assistantship Programme - it is a service commitment, not a bonus
You may not hold any other scholarship, award, fellowship or allowance, or take employment, during the scholarship without the University's prior written approval
The SGD 500 Qualifying Examination top-up is capped at the 48th month of candidature for scholars admitted from the August 2021 intake or later
No employment is guaranteed after graduation, and there is no bond, but the scholarship is tenable only at NUS and you must reside in Singapore
NUS has publicly warned that no external agent can guarantee, fast-track or directly secure postgraduate admission - apply only through the official NUS admissions route
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One GradApp admissions application with the scholarship interest flagged and the additional scholarship items completed, then faculty-level review for the August or January intake, with the scholarship renewed each semester on satisfactory progress.
